# raseeda

> raseeda is a free, private invoice generator that runs entirely in the browser. There is no account and nothing is uploaded: invoices are saved in the browser on the user's device (IndexedDB), the PDF is made on the device, and invoice content leaves it only in files the user saves. The site counts anonymous usage (event names, country, browser family, OS, device type, language, the kind of site a visit came from, and a few bucketed invoice details such as the currency code, never names or amounts) with no cookies or identifiers. It is open source under the MIT licence.

## Pages

- [Home](https://raseeda.com/): what raseeda does, how it compares with other invoice generators and accounting software, what goes on the invoice, and common questions
- [Invoice editor](https://raseeda.com/create): create, edit and download an invoice as an A4 PDF (requires JavaScript)
- [Invoice templates](https://raseeda.com/invoice-template): sample invoices for freelance, consulting, small business, contractor, photography and web development work, each opening the editor in its font
- [Privacy](https://raseeda.com/privacy): what raseeda stores, where, and what never leaves the device

## Facts

- Free, with no paid plan, no ads and no watermark on the PDF.
- No account and no sign-up.
- Any currency, VAT or sales tax, fees, discounts, payment details (bank, account and routing numbers, IBAN, BIC / SWIFT, sort code), templates for repeat clients, and import / export backups.
- raseeda makes the PDF; it does not email invoices or track payments.
- No server API and no server-side storage. In the editor, `window.raseeda` offers an on-device API for scripts and assistants driving the browser: `listInvoices()`, `getInvoice(id)`, `createInvoice(data)`, `openInvoice(id)`, `getPdf(id?)`, `downloadPdf(id?)` and `importData(json)`. Invoice data takes the shape of an export's `invoiceData`; with `tax.perLine` on, an item's own `tax: { percentage, exempt }` overrides the invoice's rate. `tableSettings.columns` (`{ quantityAndPrice, unit }`) switches the Quantity, Unit and Unit price columns off, and `tableSettings.columnLabels.tax` names the Tax column (blank uses the tax row's label) and `columnLabels.amount` the Amount column (blank reads "Net amount" with tax on, "Amount" without). `numberFormat` (`"comma-dot"`, `"dot-comma"`, `"space-comma"`, `"apostrophe-dot"` or `"indian"`) and `currencyPosition` (`"before"` or `"after"`) say how amounts are written; left out, a script's invoice is `"comma-dot"` and `"before"`. Zero-decimal currencies such as JPY are reckoned in whole units. Documented in the README.
